title: Bayesian Retrieval of L-Band Absorption by Ice using SMOS Brightness Temperatures over the Antarctic Plateau
abstract: The low absorption of microwaves at L-band in ice enables the retrieval of internal ice sheet parameters from satellite observations. However, knowing the precise value of the ice absorption $\kappa$a(T ) as a function of temperature is a strict prerequisite. The existing knowledge is well constrained above 2 GHz and under 200 MHz, lacking constraints in the P-and L-bands. In this study, we infer ice absorption values using the spatial variations of L-band radiometric observations across Antarctica and comparing them with internal ice temperature variations through a simple emission model. More importantly, we adopt a probabilistic approach to determine a credible interval for absorption, using a Bayesian retrieval method. Our algorithm seeks the optimal multiplier factor $\alpha$ to apply to the current lowest estimate ice absorption formulation $\kappa$a(T ) proposed by M{\"a}tzler 2006, and computes the probability distribution of $\alpha$. The results show the absorption is most likely 1.5 to 1.7 times higher than this lowest formulation, which reduces the actual sensing depth at L-band.

title: Generative Learning on Manifolds for Probabilistic Seismic Performance Assessment and Structural Identifiability
abstract: Seismic performance assessment relies on computationally expensive nonlinear simulations, limiting uncertainty quantification and inference of structural properties from observed responses. We develop a manifold-based generative framework that learns the joint distribution of uncertain structural parameters and seismic-response trajectories from limited high-fidelity simulations. Combining Diffusion Maps, score-based Diffusion Modeling, and Geometric Harmonics, the framework enables both forward probabilistic prediction and inverse inference. Applied to a nine-story steel moment-resisting frame, the results reveal which structural properties are identifiable from seismic performance and how uncertainty in these properties influences response. In particular, the learned representation captures post-capping degradation characteristics more effectively than individual strength parameters. Inverse inference identifies distinct structural configurations that produce similar seismic performance, with representative solutions independently validated using nonlinear simulations. These findings demonstrate how generative learning can support uncertainty-aware seismic assessment while revealing structural non-identifiability and alternative mechanisms underlying observed performance

title: First results from a borehole network for the seismic characterization of the Einstein Telescope Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site
abstract: The low-frequency sensitivity of the Einstein Telescope depends on the seismic environment of its site, both through the mechanical coupling of ground motion to the test masses and through Newtonian noise. We present the first results of the seismic characterization of the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site based on a network of recently instrumented boreholes covering the first seven months of 2026 at four underground stations and their co-located surface sensors. Two of these boreholes were deliberately sited next to railway infrastructure, so that the levels reported here describe how anthropogenic transients propagate to depth at different distances from the source. The analysis was carried out with \texttt{SiteChar}, a Python framework developed for this work to provide a common processing pipeline across different sensors, networks and observation periods. It processes the data in sequential chunks and separates the noise floor from the contribution of transients. We present a characterization of the catalogue of observed transients and a tentative classification. These measurements form part of an integrated site characterization approach that combines the observed seismic field with three-dimensional geological and wave-propagation models to predict Newtonian noise and ultimately guide its mitigation at the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site.
